ups.name: UPS
ups.lede: Live rates, labels, returns, tracking, Access Points, pickups and address validation — through the UPS OAuth REST APIs.
ups.connect: An app at developer.ups.com with your shipper account linked to it. Paste the client ID and secret, press Test connection, and a fresh token proves both.

traps.title: No PDF from the Ship API
traps.body: UPS draws GIF and ZPL. ZPL goes straight to a thermal printer; PNG is converted from UPS’s GIF with GD, and is only offered when GD is installed.

traps.title: Tokens that last an hour
traps.body: Cut from four hours on 1 April 2026. Each token is cached and a new one fetched a minute before it expires.

traps.title: One package per return
traps.body: UPS refuses multi-package returns from the US and Puerto Rico, so a multi-parcel return is stopped up front with a message saying why.

fedex.name: FedEx
fedex.lede: Live rates, labels in four formats, returns, tracking, Hold at Location, pickups and address validation — through the FedEx REST APIs.
fedex.connect: A project at developer.fedex.com with your account linked. The environment must match the keys — FedEx issues separate ones for its sandbox and for production.

traps.title: Ground is two services
traps.body: FEDEX_GROUND to a business, GROUND_HOME_DELIVERY to a home. The right one is sent for each address and reported under the service the method asked for.

traps.title: Hold at Location, never residential
traps.body: A pickup-point method ships with Hold at Location for the counter the customer chose, and is never charged as a residential delivery.

traps.title: Up to 40 packages, one shipment
traps.body: One tracking number and one label per package, under a master number that voids the whole shipment at once.

usps.name: USPS
usps.lede: Prices, domestic, international and return labels, tracking, pickups and Hold for Pickup — on the USPS APIs v3, not the retired Web Tools.
usps.connect: A developer-portal app for the API calls, plus your CRID, MID and payment account from the Business Customer Gateway for labels. Test reads which APIs the app was granted.

traps.title: Labels need a second token
traps.body: A payment token minted from your CRID, MID and EPS account, cached per connection and per account — so a changed account never pays with the old one.

traps.title: One package at a time
traps.body: USPS has no shipment grouping. If package 2 fails, package 1 is voided; if that void isn’t clean, the shipment is uncertain and lists every number bought.

traps.title: 60 calls an hour
traps.body: USPS’s default quota. Every class is priced in one call, once per distinct package — keep Carrier’s rate cache on.

freight.name: LTL Freight
freight.tagline: Six LTL carriers, wired into Craft Commerce.
freight.lede: TForce Freight, Old Dominion, Estes, XPO, R+L and SAIA — quotes, bills of lading, PRO tracking and, where the API allows, pickups.
freight.connect: Each carrier wants something different — Azure AD client credentials for TForce, a portal login for ODFL, three product keys for SAIA. Each connection asks for exactly its own.

traps.title: Freight class is a string
traps.body: “77.5” and “92.50” pass; “77” is refused. No class and no default? The shipment is refused, naming the handling unit. Nothing is guessed.

traps.title: Residential only when you say so
traps.body: Taken from the residential accessorials — never from the address flag, which defaults to true at checkout and costs a fee on LTL.

traps.title: A BOL without a PRO is uncertain
traps.body: A bill of lading accepted before a PRO is assigned is not a refusal. It waits for a person instead of a second BOL being bought.

dpd.name: DPD
dpd.lede: DPD Croatia and DPD Slovenia through DPD’s own EasyShip — labels, cash on delivery, parcel shops, collections and the daily manifest.
dpd.connect: Your EasyShip portal login — DPD issues no separate API key. That is easyship.hr or easyship.si, not the unrelated Easyship.com aggregator.

traps.title: Labels vanish after two minutes
traps.body: After that, EasyShip returns an empty PDF. The label is fetched in the same purchase that creates the parcel, and Carrier keeps those bytes.

traps.title: No parcel-shop API
traps.body: Ask DPD for the PUDO list and import it as CSV. Imported points only change when you change them, and EasyShip’s required fields are checked before sending.

traps.title: House numbers kept apart
traps.body: “Ilica 242a” is split automatically and Croatian “bb” is understood. An address with no number is refused before anything is sent.

gls.name: GLS
gls.lede: MyGLS in Croatia, Hungary, Czechia, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia and Serbia — labels, cash on delivery, shops and lockers, batch reprints and tracking.
gls.connect: The country your GLS contract is with — each runs its own MyGLS — and the username, password and client number you already use there.

traps.title: A wrong password answers 200
traps.body: MyGLS reports bad credentials inside a successful response. The connection test reads it and says “MyGLS refused the username or password”.

traps.title: Lockers need three contacts
traps.body: GLS refuses parcel-shop and locker parcels without a name, phone and email, so all three are checked before anything is sent.

traps.title: A picker that never empties
traps.body: Every shop and locker is synced daily from GLS’s map feed. If the feed ever breaks, the last good sync is kept rather than an empty picker.

boxnow.name: BOX NOW
boxnow.tagline: BOX NOW lockers, wired into Craft Commerce.
boxnow.lede: Greece, Cyprus, Bulgaria, Croatia and Slovenia — locker delivery, cash on delivery, labels, cancellation, tracking and the whole locker list.
boxnow.connect: The partner client ID and secret BOX NOW issued for your country, and your warehouse id. Got the warehouse wrong? Test lists the right ones.

traps.title: An order number, once
traps.body: BOX NOW never accepts a number twice, even after a cancel. Carrier sends the reference plus a hash of the shipment, so a retry can’t deliver twice.

traps.title: Phones must be international
traps.body: National numbers are completed with the connection country’s code. The PIN goes out by SMS and email, so name, phone and email are all required.

traps.title: The smallest compartment that fits
traps.body: 20 kg a parcel and three compartment heights. The size is chosen from each parcel’s own dimensions.

posts.name: National Posts
posts.tagline: Four national posts, wired into Craft Commerce.
posts.lede: Hrvatska pošta, Pošta Slovenije, Magyar Posta and ELTA Courier — labels, cash on delivery, Paketomat and PostaPont points, tracking and the end-of-day close.
posts.connect: None of these APIs is open to the public. Every post issues its own credentials with your contract, and each connection asks only for its own.

traps.title: Magyar Posta ships nothing until the day is closed
traps.body: Close the day from the connection and the posting list is stored. After that MPL can’t void or reprint, so do both first.

traps.title: Hrvatska pošta caps e-mail at 25 characters
traps.body: A longer address is left off and the shipment warns — cutting an address short would make it wrong.

traps.title: No home-made labels for Pošta Slovenije
traps.body: Its API returns no label or tracking number, so the driver offers tracking and points only, never a label refused at the counter.

posts.honestLede: Nothing here has run against a live account. Hrvatska pošta and Magyar Posta are checked against their own documentation (high confidence); Pošta Slovenije is low–medium and ELTA low.
